articles.title: Festival Transformar em Santos: Programação gratuita até domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: A programação reúne oficinas de fotografia, teatro, gastronomia e sustentabilidade, além de exposições, apresentações culturais e uma feira com mais de 60 marcas. As atividades são gratuitas e acontecem no Sesc Santos e na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva, até domingo (15).
articles.summary: O Festival Transformar Santos oferece oficinas de fotografia, gastronomia e feira criativa com 60 marcas na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro e no Sesc até este domingo.
articles.body:
Também será possível participar de uma oficina que acompanhará os bastidores do 'Documentário Transformar' — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Santos

A cidade de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, recebe até domingo (15) a terceira edição do Festival Transformar, com programação gratuita voltada à cultura, educação, sustentabilidade e economia criativa. Entre as atrações, há oficinas, apresentações culturais, exposições e uma feira com mais de 60 marcas.

Idealizado por Gabriel Del Corso e realizado pela Re-Set.br, o festival tem o apoio do Senac Santos e do Sesc Santos. O Instituto Brasileiro de Defesa da Natureza (IBDN) é parceiro nas ações de neutralização de carbono.

A programação começou na quarta-feira (11), com atividades no Sesc Santos, no bairro Aparecida, e na Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva. Entre os destaques, estão oficinas de fotografia, teatro, customização de roupas, gastronomia e alimentação saudável.

As atividades são gratuitas e têm vagas limitadas. A programação é dividida entre o Sesc Santos, na Rua Conselheiro Ribas, nº 136, e a Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva, ambos no bairro Aparecida.

As inscrições para as oficinas do Senac estão disponíveis no site da instituição. As demais atividades têm inscrições e condições específicas de participação.

O núcleo Mar Aberto — Futuros em Circulação oferece atividades em diferentes áreas. Confira alguns dos temas:

Customização de roupas e reaproveitamento de tecidos;

Culinária caiçara e alimentação saudável;

Laboratório audiovisual para produção de minidocumentários;

Painel sobre desenvolvimento sustentável e governança colaborativa.

Até sábado (14), das 11h às 21h, a Praça Dr. Caio Ribeiro de Moraes e Silva recebe o núcleo Viva Circular, com mais de 60 marcas de gastronomia, arte, moda, design e outros segmentos.

O espaço também terá exposições, música, atividades culturais gratuitas e iniciativas de afroempreendedorismo do Coletivo AfroTu.

Unidade Sesc Santos. — Foto: Divulgação/Sesc

articles.title: Kathy Ireland’s husband escapes burning boat after engine explodes 20 miles offshore
articles.summary: Kathy Ireland shared dramatic footage of husband Greg Olsen's boat engulfed in flames after an engine explosion 20 miles west of Santa Barbara.
articles.body: Kathy Ireland is thankful after her husband narrowly escaped a fire that engulfed his boat while he was alone at sea. In a recent Instagram post, the 63-year-old actress shared video of husband Dr. Greg Olsen's boat, the 4th Watch, engulfed in flames. Ireland said Olsen was out alone on the water while she was away on business. "Life is really hard and really beautiful. God is great," she wrote. "Engine exploded and a fire quickly melted all navigation equipment and survival raft!" She then thanked everyone "who prayed and continue to pray" for her husband, as well as all "those who aided in the rescue," including "@towboatus_ventura and the entire community" for their quick response. KATHY IRELAND REVEALS 'BIG RED FLAG' THAT EXPOSED ALLEGED $100M 'UNCONSCIONABLE' BETRAYAL "Most of all, we thank our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ for this miracle of his survival," she added. Ireland also shared a note she wrote to her husband following the incident, saying her "heart is both heavy and full" because she knows how much "love, sweat and life you poured into this vessel." "This vessel brought so much joy and so many blessings to our family and countless others," she continued. "My heart is heavy with yours. This is more than a boat, there are many implications. My heart is mostly full. Full because of the outpouring of love and support. Multitudes were praying for you! I’m so thankful to all who rushed to pray and come to your rescue." "I’m so thankful God gifted you with a brilliant mind to navigate this disaster so seamlessly," she added. "I’m eternally thankful to Him for loving and rescuing you. Though the vessel is no more, the 4th Watch is forever. You named that boat so profoundly. He has so much ahead for you! I’m so proud of you." WATCH: KATHY IRELAND SHARES THE LESSONS SHE'S LEARNED FROM WORKING AS A COMMERCIAL FISHERMAN Fans in the comments section shared well-wishes for Ireland and Olsen, with some recounting their own experiences with losing their belongings due to a fire. "Unbelievable!!! I’m SO grateful your husband is ok," one fan wrote. "🙏 And having parents who lost their home in a fire I completely understand your sadness about the loss of the boat. " "Oh my! I am so glad he is safe," another added. "The boat and gear is replaceable, but the emotions are real. So sorry!!!!" A third follower wrote, "So sorry to hear this, BUT, Thankful to God that he saved your Precious One!" GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The TowBoatUS Ventura Instagram account also shared video of the fire and its aftermath, saying the company received a call about the fire around 3 p.m. on Wednesday afternoon, noting the vessel was "20 nautical miles west of Santa Barbara Harbor." In its post, TowBoatUS Ventura credited Olsen for his quick thinking, noting that he "was prepared and did everything right." They wrote that he initially "attempted to extinguish the fire before ultimately activating his EPIRB and abandoning ship into a kayak." "This was about as good an outcome as one could hope for in an otherwise serious emergency," the message read. "A well-prepared mariner, good samaritans nearby, and commercial vessels equipped and ready to respond made all the difference. It is a great reminder of the importance of preparedness, cooperation, and the maritime community looking out for one another." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' box office collection day 10: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash's film earns over 3 times 'Animal'; crosses Rs 1,200 cr worldwide; Hindi version leads
articles.summary: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continues its impressive theatrical run, recording a major jump in collections on its second
articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continues its impressive theatrical run, recording a major jump in collections on its second Saturday. The mythological epic collected Rs 72.90 cr net in India on Day 10, registering a 51.6% rise over the previous day's earnings. With this, the film's domestic net collection has reached Rs 685.60 cr, while its India gross stands at Rs 819.50 cr. The film has also crossed the Rs 1,200 cr milestone worldwide, with its cumulative gross collection reaching Rs 1,228 cr.Ramayana Movie Review'Ramayana' Day 10 box office collection across languagesAccording to Sacnilk, the Hindi version remained the biggest contributor to the film's Saturday earnings. It collected Rs 53.75 cr from 18,557 shows. The Kannada version followed with Rs 5.40 cr from 893 screenings. Both Malayalam and Tamil versions earned Rs 4.75 cr each, from 1,127 and 1,290 shows, respectively. Telugu contributed another Rs 4.25 cr through 1,584 screenings.Across all five languages, the film registered an overall occupancy of 45.5% on Saturday. Malayalam recorded the highest occupancy at 83%, followed by Tamil at 62.5% and Kannada at 58.8%. Hindi registered 41.9%, while Telugu recorded 39.1%.For the Hindi 3D version, overall occupancy stood at 53%. Morning shows recorded 30.08%, while afternoon screenings reached 57.08%. Evening shows registered 62.77% occupancy, followed by 62.08% during the night.'Ramayana' worldwide box office collection crosses Rs 1,200 crThe film's overseas performance has further strengthened its global box office position. International markets contributed Rs 30 cr on Day 10, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 408.50 cr. Combined with its domestic gross, the worldwide collection has reached Rs 1,228 cr, according to Sacnilk.The domestic market accounts for 66.7% of the worldwide earnings, while overseas territories contribute the remaining 33.3%. The film's average collection per show on Saturday was Rs 32,454. Its latest performance also marks a considerable improvement over Friday, when it earned Rs 48.10 cr net in India.'Ramayana' box office collection: Day-wise performance'Ramayana' began its theatrical journey on November 5 with Rs 64.85 cr net in India. After collecting Rs 48.05 cr on Friday, the film recovered on Saturday with Rs 69.80 cr. Sunday brought in Rs 56.15 cr before Monday delivered its biggest single-day collection of Rs 107.50 cr.The film subsequently earned Rs 94.10 cr on Tuesday and Rs 70.65 cr on Wednesday. Its first Thursday collection stood at Rs 53.50 cr. The opening eight-day run generated Rs 564.60 cr net and Rs 675.05 cr gross domestically.Friday's earnings during the second week stood at Rs 48.10 cr. Saturday's improved performance pushed the two-day second-week total to Rs 121 cr net and Rs 144.45 cr gross. The Hindi version has contributed Rs 527.25 cr to the domestic net collection so far, accounting for 76.9% of the total. Kannada follows with Rs 57.35 cr, while Telugu has generated Rs 44.90 cr. Tamil and Malayalam have contributed Rs 29.65 cr and Rs 26.45 cr, respectively.Ranbir Kapoor's 'Ramayana' earns over three times 'Animal'The latest figures also put the film ahead of Ranbir Kapoor's previous release, 'Animal', at the same stage of its theatrical run. Directed by Sandeep Reddy Vanga, the action drama collected Rs 36 cr net in India on its tenth day. This is less than half of 'Ramayana's' corresponding domestic earnings.'Animal' recorded Rs 33.53 cr from its Hindi version, with 12,949 shows. Telugu contributed Rs 2.13 cr through 1,168 screenings, while Tamil added Rs 30 lakh from 222 shows. Kannada and Malayalam each earned Rs 2 lakh, from 17 and 34 screenings, respectively.By Day 10, 'Animal' had accumulated Rs 431.27 cr net and Rs 514.05 cr gross in India. Its overseas gross stood at Rs 203.25 cr, including Rs 13.75 cr from the tenth day. The worldwide gross collection reached Rs 717.30 cr. Its second-week earnings had reached Rs 93.69 cr, with the tenth day contributing Rs 36 cr.About 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend''Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' brings the timeless Indian epic about Lord Rama and King Ravana to the screen through a contemporary cinematic adaptation. The story has influenced generations and remains deeply rooted in India's cultural traditions.The first instalment focuses on Prince Rama's early life and the challenges he encounters as the rightful heir to Ayodhya. Headlined by Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, the ambitious film revisits the legendary narrative through modern Indian cinema.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. All figures are approximate unless explicitly mentioned, offering a fair representation of the movie's box office performance. These totals may change as official studio data is updated or as additional international market reports are finalized. KRISTIN CAVALLARI FLAUNTS HER TONED FIGURE IN BIKINIS DURING EUROPEAN SUMMER VACATION Cavallari added that she is now looking forward to turning 40, saying, "If this is what 40s is, like f- - - yeah. This is fun." Earlier in the episode, the "Very Cavallari" star quipped that it "takes one to two years of abstinence to become a nun" and that she is on her way towards that achievement. articles.title: Parenting advice by Khloé Kardashian: 'It's so important for kids to know, to see how adults trip or fail a little bit,' reveals the diva, explaining how she stopped her daughter from quitting gymnastics
articles.summary: Discover how Khloé Kardashian inspired her daughter True to keep pursuing gymnastics despite struggles, emphasizing the importance of showing kids that even adults can fail and learn.
articles.body: Khloé Kardashian wasn't about to let her daughter give up gymnastics over one cartwheel. True, who is eight, was frustrated because she couldn't nail the move, and she kept comparing herself to her cousins, who seemed to be doing much better. So Khloé came up with a plan. She'd try a cartwheel herself, fully expecting to fail at it too.She told the story on an episode of her podcast, Khloé in Wonder Land, with actor Goldie Hawn as her guest. They were discussing parenting and kids' confidence, and Khloé described how her own clumsy attempt ended up changing True's mind.Why did True Thompson want to quit gymnastics?According to Khloé Kardashian, True was thinking about giving up because her cousins could do the cartwheel better than she could. It was really getting to her, especially watching the other kids manage something she was stuck on.So Khloé said she'd go to gymnastics and try as well. She wanted True to see that even grown-ups can't do everything, and that nothing is embarrassing about that. Here's how she remembered putting it to her daughter: "Girl, do you want to? Okay. I'm going to go to gymnastics with you. I'm going to do a cartwheel because I can't do one. And I'm going to show her that an adult can't do this. And you're going to be fine."Khloé Kardashian's cartwheel attempt made True more confidentShe did go through with it, and it sounds like it didn't go to plan. She was laughing about it on the podcast, saying, "So I did a cartwheel the best I could. It was silly. I looked ridiculous."That was enough to make True feel better about her own effort. Watching her mum struggle with the same move made her realise she wasn't as bad at it as she'd thought.And it worked. Khloé Kardashian said True kept going with gymnastics for another three years after that. In her words: "She now has been in gymnastics three years longer because she saw how ridiculous I looked and she looked way better than me. So she has all this confidence."Khloé Kardashian on why parents should let children see them failThe chat with Goldie Hawn moved on to why parents don't need to look perfect in front of their children. Khloé Kardashian thinks kids should see adults mess up and, just as importantly, see what they do next. She said, "It's so important, I think, for kids to know, to see how adults trip or fail a little bit. Like, how do we handle that?"The gymnastics story is a pretty good example. She didn't give True another pep talk about trying harder. She just made herself the example, couldn't do the cartwheel either, and was happy to laugh at herself about it.Khloé Kardashian says daughter True won't get social media anytime soonKhloé Kardashian also talked about the rules she's set around phones and social media. True is eight and doesn't have a phone, and Khloé has no plans to let her on social media any time soon. "My daughter's only eight, but she's not getting social media for a very long time. She doesn't even have a phone," she said.She also sounded a bit baffled by how young some kids are when they get their first phone. "Kids these days have phones at eight. I'm like, who are you calling? I don't understand," she added.Khloé shares True and her four-year-old son, Tatum Thompson, with her ex Tristan Thompson. She's talked about different parts of raising the two of them before, and this time it was one small moment from True's gymnastics classes that came up.Khloé didn't get the cartwheel, but True got something out of watching her try. She stuck with gymnastics, and her mum came away with a pretty funny story.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Blake Lively’s beverage venture winds down after five years; sales concerns emerge amid Justin Baldoni legal battle - Reports
articles.summary: Blake Lively’s beverage business is reportedly heading towards closure, nearly five years after the actress introduced her drinks venture.
articles.body: Blake Lively’s beverage business is reportedly heading towards closure, nearly five years after the actress introduced her drinks venture. The company operates Betty Buzz, a non-alcoholic beverage brand, and its alcoholic counterpart, Betty Booze. Recent developments surrounding the business have raised questions about its future, including inactive social media accounts and changes to its trademark portfolio.According to PEOPLE, the company is winding down its operations and is expected to cease business. The Betty Buzz website is no longer accessible, while the Betty Booze website remained operational as of November 10. The latter continues to showcase its products, although the overall status of the business remains unclear.The reported development follows a series of changes involving the company's online presence and intellectual property filings. While these developments have fuelled speculation about a possible shutdown, the available reports alone do not confirm that the business has officially closed.Beverage venture face uncertain futureBlake Lively launched the beverage venture with two distinct product lines. Both brands were introduced as part of the actress's move into the consumer products market.However, the company's digital presence has changed considerably. The Betty Buzz website is now unavailable, while Betty Booze continues to maintain an active website. The difference has attracted attention amid reports that the business is preparing to wind down.PEOPLE reported that the company is expected to stop operating. Neither the continued availability of the Betty Booze website nor the status of its products necessarily indicates that the brand will remain in business.Several trademark applications abandonedTMZ reported on November 4 that multiple trademark applications associated with Blake Lively's beverage company had been abandoned. The filings were made after the business was launched and covered several categories of products.These included beer-based beverages, non-alcoholic carbonated drinks and other products. However, the trademarks for Betty Buzz and Betty Booze remain active, according to the report.For the unversed, abandoned applications do not automatically mean that a company has ceased operations. Likewise, active registrations for the two principal brands do not establish whether their products will continue to be sold.Instagram accounts show reduced activityThe company's social media presence has also become less frequent. Betty Booze's Instagram account last published an update on September 28, 2026. Betty Buzz's account has been inactive since April 5, 2026.The lack of recent posts, combined with the Betty Buzz website becoming inaccessible, has prompted further questions about the brands' operations. Justin Baldoni legal battle draws attentionThe reported wind-down comes amid Blake Lively's ongoing legal dispute with actor-director Justin Baldoni, her co-star in 'It Ends With Us'. The case has generated considerable public attention, and the negative publicity surrounding the actress is believed to have affected the beverage business.An internal document that became public during the legal proceedings reportedly showed significant sales declines for both Betty Buzz and Betty Booze in August 2024. The figures highlighted the commercial difficulties faced by the brands during that period.According to Inc., retail buyers had also expressed concerns about the potential impact of the controversy surrounding Lively on the beverage lines. While the extent of the damage to sales remains unclear, the reported concerns suggest that the publicity became a factor in how retailers viewed the business.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Former DC head James Gunn shuts down 'Man of Tomorrow' editing rumours, says no Skydance executive has seen the film: 'Any stories around this narrative are false'
articles.summary: James Gunn refutes rumors that Skydance executives demanded changes to the upcoming Superman sequel 'Man of Tomorrow', confirming they haven't seen the film yet.
articles.body: James Gunn has pushed back on rumours about his upcoming DC film 'Man of Tomorrow'. Reports had been circulating that Skydance executives watched the Superman sequel and asked for big changes, but Gunn says that simply isn’t true. As he put it, no one from the company has seen the movie yet, so there’s been no screening and no notes.Gunn addressed the discussion in a post on Threads on November 13, following the announcement that he and Peter Safran would step away from their leadership positions at DC Studios. The news raised questions among fans about the future of projects developed under their management, particularly the next chapter of Superman's story.“There are a lot of untrue rumours going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen ‘Man of Tomorrow’ and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made,” Gunn wrote.“No one from Skydance has even seen the movie – the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false. ”What rumours surrounded 'Man of Tomorrow'?Speculation about the film intensified after reports suggested that the incoming studio leadership could request significant changes to Gunn's sequel. Online discussions included claims about possible reshoots, removed character appearances, and changes to the filmmaker's creative control.Some of the rumours also raised questions about the involvement of characters connected to the wider DC Universe, including Supergirl and Blue Beetle. However, these claims were not confirmed by DC Studios or Skydance.Gunn's response specifically addressed the suggestion that Skydance executives had already watched the film and ordered a major overhaul. By saying who has actually seen the film, Gunn shot down that narrative. He didn’t promise anything about future studio decisions, but he did push back on claims that executives had already stepped into the editing process.Why are James Gunn and Peter Safran leaving DC Studios?The rumours surfaced at a significant time for DC Studios. Big news landed on November 9: Skydance announced that Gunn and Peter Safran are leaving their posts after four years in charge of the division. They’ll officially be out on December 1, 2026. Former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham will take over as president and chief creative officer. He will oversee the studio's film, television and animation projects and report to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein.In its official announcement, Skydance said Gunn and Safran would return full-time to their creative work. Gunn and Safran also said they still want to keep telling stories they care about, including the next chapter of Clark Kent and Lex Luthor’s story in 'Man of Tomorrow'.Their departure from executive positions does not mean they are leaving the film behind. Gunn remains its writer and director, while he and Safran are attached as producers.What is 'Man of Tomorrow' about?'Man of Tomorrow' is the follow-up to Gunn’s 2025 film 'Superman'. It continues Clark Kent and Lex Luthor’s story, with the two rivals teaming up against a bigger threat. David Corenswet returns as Superman, and Nicholas Hoult is back as Lex Luthor.The film also introduces Lars Eidinger as Brainiac, a major antagonist from DC Comics. Rachel Brosnahan is returning as Lois Lane, alongside other familiar faces from the previous film.The production completed principal photography in August 2026, with Gunn confirming the wrap through his social media. The film is now in post-production and is scheduled to arrive in theatres on July 9, 2027, according to the official announcement.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
